design_tradeoffs: A local kernel lock cannot coordinate different login hosts. The shared claim is a separate no-follow exclusive publication, and remote active owners remain uncertain until inspected.
Two separated verified controller reads can establish unique one-shot request absence; missing accounting alone never proves cleanup.
Forking is confined to the single-threaded Linux worker, preserving subprocess fallback and fresh task resource limits.

SQLite claim and result publication remain separate short transactions. Holding one transaction across scheduler I/O would block unrelated admissions and compromise cancellation; WAL/NORMAL plus thread-local connection reuse removes redundant setup/durability cost.
Remote cache stages immutable bounded content by digest; it adds several cold first-host processes but warm reads avoid source retransmission and recompilation.
design_tradeoffs_latest: Blank-profile reuse adds one bounded validation read; explicit profile path preserves its existing read count, and launch still rechecks actual controller identity.

No-cgroup placement adds one local listpids read only when required; cgroup-proof path remains two reads. Lack of local slurmd capability stays unverified instead of assuming allocation environment implies membership.

MCP cancellation reuses the existing socket wake primitive; task cancel and reaping remain owned by the serialized executor. No extra perpetual poller, scheduler read or automatic replay is introduced.
SQL subprocess isolation preserves all tighter inherited limits and returns actual setup failures as structured errors; limits are not raised to make tests pass.
